object.name: evi.lpg~
object.digest: Buchla Lowpass Gate emulation for your west coast synthesis fun
object.description: Circuit modelled emulation of the Buchla Lowpass-Gate, unique version of a two-pole Sallen and Key filter, based on 'A Digital Model of the Buchla Lowpass-Gate' by Julian Parker and Stefano DAngelo, 2013 . In evieve this has been heavily modified from the original paper. Control is all audio rate inputs to the voltage input to the gate, with additional features such as extra feedback resistors (<m>boom</m> ) and simultaneous filter outputs.
object.discussion: The code of this abstraction can also be used entirely inside gen~ / GenExpr by using the <o>evi_lpg_buchla</o>.gendsp abstraction (which has internal oversampling) and <o>evi_control_lpg_buchla</o>.gendsp for control. See the 'gen~' tab of the helpfile for details.

inlets.description: Audio input to be filtered / gated.
Audio rate ping to attack the filter gate.
Filter resonance. Effect also depends on other settings, especially @boom and @lpg.
Offset (add to) the voltage input to the LPG, thus increasing the starting point of the LPG filter sweep. Part of the control circuit that engages the voltage (frequency) of the filter/gate.
Scale (multiply) the voltage input to the LPG, thus extending the frequency range of the LPG filter sweep. Part of the control circuit that engages the voltage (frequency) of the filter/gate.

Amount of sweep range of the voltage input to the LPG, from a small range to a large range. Can be used as a classic sounding Lowpass filter cutoff sweeper. Part of the control circuit that engages the voltage (frequency) of the filter/gate.

outlets.description: Quirky bandpass version of the gate. Also very effective.
Quirky highpass version of the gate. Somewhat experimental and needs (gain) massaging.

outlets.digest: Envelope, switch with @envout 1 = Vactrol (default), @envout 0 = Control Circuit
outlets.description: Aux output of the control envelope follower that modifies the ping of the LPG. Can be useful for synchronous downstream processing. See the @envout attribute for envelope selection.

arguments.name: upsample
arguments.description: Oversampling factor for the core filter algorithm. Can be 2, 4 or 8. Default 4. Can only be a typed in argument.

arguments.name: resonance
arguments.description: Sets the initially used resonance amount (inlet 3) for if setting up a static filter. Note this is no use if later connecting a signal, as the arg would then act as an offset.

attributes.name: boom
attributes.description: Core filter/gate functionality. Only has effect if the @lpg attribute is > zero. Smoothly crossfades additional resistors into the feedback path of the LPG while maintaining filter stability. This can have a drastic effect on the tone of the filter and the resonance behaviour. It is also directly affected by the resonance value. If @lpg and @boom are both high (or '1') and @vca is low (or '0') you will achieve that classic squelchy whooping LPG behaviour.

attributes.name: envout
attributes.description: Selects an envelope type to be output by the 4th (far right) outlet of the abstraction. If @envout == 1 (the default) the vactrol envelope is output. If @envout == 0, the 'Rf' (frequency control voltage) envelope is output, which are very large voltage values.

attributes.name: leakage
attributes.description: Controls the amplitude signal outputs. If @leakage = 0 (the default) the audio outputs of the object are zeroed when the amplitude of the vactrol envelope reaches below a certain gain level set by the @threshold attribute (default -60 dB). If @leakage = 1 no attempt is made to silence the outputs, often resulting in constant low level audio, as can happen in an analog system.

attributes.name: lpg
attributes.description: Core filter/gate functionality. Smoothly switch or interpolate between (lowpass) filter and gate behaviour. Typically this is set to '1', but can be very useful when wanting to dial in the effect of the gate. Different gate and VCA effects can be achieved by modifying this along with the @vca attribute.

attributes.name: nonlin
attributes.description: Turning this off is atypical behaviour. It is strongly advised not to turn this off. On (the default) engages the nonlinearities in the filter/gate structure. However, it can be interesting triggering it linearly, but if you do so be careful of overall gain - if off there are no safeguards for the resonance (inlet 3) or @boom attribute settings.

attributes.name: offsetsmooth
attributes.description: Smooth the control 'offset' inlet (inlet 4). Useful if using floats on that inlet. Turn off (set to 0) if modulating inlet 4 at audio rate.

attributes.name: override
attributes.description: A special option which simplifies the LPG interaction. If set to on (1) the vactrol envelope controls all 'control inlets' (inlets 4, 5 and 6). This forces a classic LPG sound in a simple way. Typically, when using this feature, one would switch inlets 4, 5 and 6 to zero and control the LPG only via the @vactrol... attributes. However, the vactrol 'override' control is summed with the control inlets, so interesting effects can be achieved by utilising 'scale' (inlet 5) and 'sweep' (inlet 6) simultaneously (but 'offset' - inlet 4 - is easier to use if set to zero with the 'override' feature on, although there is no harm in trying). If @override is off (the default), the LPG behaves as normal, with the control inlets only tuned by the values at their inputs.

attributes.name: response
attributes.description: Subtle. This control switches between short..long response times for the voltage input into the control circuit shaper. It is only noticeable with strong @lpg and resonance settings (including @boom).

attributes.name: scalesmooth
attributes.description: Smooth the control scale inlet (inlet 5). Useful if using floats on that inlet. Turn off (set to 0) if modulating inlet 5 at audio rate.

attributes.name: smooth
attributes.description: Smoothing time in ms for the interpolated @vca, @lpg and @boom attributes.

attributes.name: sweepsmooth
attributes.description: Smooth the control sweep inlet (inlet 6). Useful if using floats on that inlet. Turn off (set to 0) if modulating inlet 6 at audio rate.

attributes.name: threshold
attributes.description: If the @leakage attribute is set to '0' (the default), @threshold sets the vactrol envelope gain level in dB below which the audio output signals are zeroed. If @leakage = 1 this attribute is ignored.

attributes.name: vactroldecay
attributes.description: The relative decay time of the initial vactrol envelope, 0..1 fast..slow, default 0.5 . Higher values give the vactrol envelope a slow(er) and less dynamic response feeling. Lower values can become very snappy and even clicky. Tune in conjunction with the @vactrolshape attribute, which operates in the y range as oposed to the x range of @vactroldecay.

attributes.name: vactrolgate
attributes.description: Transforms the behaviour of how the LPG attack stage behaves. If set to '0', fast repeated triggers result in dynamic variable 'ping' maximums, resulting in a novel 'build up' effect. At 0..4 this effect becomes less pronounced until when set at '5' (the default) the attack behaviour of the LPG is predictable and repeatable with normalised maximums for every trigger. If set greater than about 20 the flattening of the ping maximums become more pronounced resulting in atttack 'hold' behaviours clamping the maximum. The effects of this @vactrolgate attribute are unique to the evieve LPG and mimic certain types of analog behaviours.

attributes.name: vactrolmapdamp
attributes.description: Low shelving filter damp, optionally maps between V_c (vactrol) and V_b (filter cutoff voltage). 0 = no damping (default, bypassed), 1 = fully damped. Under the right settings, this attribute can have a strong affect on the attack feeling of the gate voltage. A higher damping value 'softens' the attack at the filter stage rather than in the envelope stage. This can add a squidgy sound that is rather cool. The mapping filter frequency is set by the @vactrolmaphz attribute.

attributes.name: vactrolmaphz
attributes.description: Low shelving filter frequency, optionally maps between V_c (vactrol) and V_b (filter cutoff voltage). Typically this would be set to low Hz values (perhaps 5..20) for maximum effect. This filter mapping is controlled by the @vactrolmapdamp attribute and is by default off.

attributes.name: vactrolscalar
attributes.description: Scale the output amplitude of the vactrol envelope at the beginning of the ping chain. Very different behaviours can be achieved by modifying this in combination with careful tuning if the @vactroldecay and @vactrolshape attributes. LPG scaling behaviour is achieved with the 'Offset', 'Scale' and 'Sweep' controls (inlets 4, 5 and 6), but it is possible to use @vactrolscalar to interact with those settings' behaviours to achieve different sorts of effects. This attribute can also require high settings when using the @override attribute feature.

attributes.name: vactrolshape
attributes.description: Transform the vactrol envelope shape between flat ('0') and sharp ('1'). This has a radical affect on the sound of the ping. Higher values also accentuate the attack stage and increase the amplitude of the envelope hitting the LPG, especially if @vactrolgate is low.

attributes.name: vca
attributes.description: Core filter/gate functionality. Smoothly switch or interpolate between LP(G) and VCA behaviour. Using the object as a pure VCA is useful but far less fun. If @lpg is high, this can be thought of as a gate damping effect, darkening the tone. If @lpg is low (or off), this controls the hardness of the VCA attack, with best 'vca'-like results achieved with @vca slightly less than '1' (at '1' the VCA is very dull).
